keyAndScale.modalCharacter: A Aeolian (Natural Minor) for the haunting clean arpeggio verse, shifting into uplifting C Major and G Mixolydian power chords on the chorus

scalesUsed.name: A Natural Minor (Aeolian)
scalesUsed.notes: A - B - C - D - E - F - G
scalesUsed.application: Drives the somber, cascading clean guitar arpeggio intro and moody verse dynamic build

scalesUsed.name: C Major / Ionian
scalesUsed.notes: C - D - E - F - G - A - B
scalesUsed.application: Forms the harmonic explosion in the chorus, lifting the song into soaring anthemic territory

scalesUsed.name: A Minor Pentatonic
scalesUsed.application: Foundation for Rick Brewster's singing, melodic solo passages and screaming high-register bends

mainProgression.description: Hypnotic descending Andalusian/Aeolian progression transitioning from delicate clean arpeggios into thunderous crunch

sectionProgressions.description: Cascading finger-style or alternate-picked arpeggios with ringing open strings creating cinematic Australian atmosphere
Explosive shift to major tonality with wide-open Marshall power chords and soaring vocal harmonies
Driving rhythm section supporting Rick Brewster's soaring, emotionally charged guitar solo

harmonicFunction: Am (Tonic i): Melancholic home key grounding the song in deep Australian emotional resonance
G (Subtonic ♭VII): Steps smoothly downward providing modal motion without classical leading-tone tension
F (Submediant ♭VI): Dramatic harmonic low point creating powerful longing before turning around
C (Relative Major ♭III): Breaks the tension in the chorus with a burst of sunlight and anthemic release

techniques.name: Arpeggiated Cross-String Picking
techniques.description: Delicate, articulate alternate picking across non-adjacent strings while holding chord shapes

notes: Hold the full Am, G, and F chord shapes firmly so ringing strings don't choke out
Keep picking strokes light and fluid with a thin or medium pick
Let each note ring into the next to build a rich harmonic wash

techniques.name: Extreme Dynamic Switching
techniques.description: Mastering the dramatic contrast between whispering clean arpeggios and explosive hard rock crunch

notes: Roll guitar volume down or switch to a clean channel for the verses
Kick in overdrive or roll volume to 10 on the first beat of the chorus
Dig in with aggressive pick attack to make the chorus hit like a hammer

sections.name: Haunting Chime Arpeggio Intro
sections.description: The instantly recognizable clean electric guitar arpeggios that define the moody Australian intro
notes: Pick cleanly across the A, D, G, B, and high E strings
Maintain absolute rhythmic consistency on every eighth note
Add subtle chorus and delay for expansive stereo width

sections.name: Dynamic Verse Build
sections.description: The rhythm section enters underneath the arpeggios, tightening the groove with subtle palm muting
notes: Introduce light palm muting on the lower strings while keeping the higher notes clear
Accentuate beats 2 and 4 to lock with the snare drum
Gradually open up the muting as the verse approaches the chorus

sections.name: Explosive Hard Rock Chorus Riff
sections.description: The song erupts into crushing Marshall crunch, modulating to C Major for a triumphant release
notes: Switch pickup or kick on high-gain overdrive on beat 1
Hit the C5 and G5 power chords with full right-hand commitment
Let each chord sustain for two full beats to give the vocals room to soar

sections.name: Soaring Melodic Solo
sections.description: Rick Brewster delivers one of his most melodic, lyrical guitar solos, blending classical phrasing with hard rock bite
notes: Initiate the solo with a patient, singing note choice on the B string
Execute smooth whole-step bends up to the high E and A root notes
Apply wide, classical-style finger vibrato on sustained notes

guitar.recommended: Fender Stratocaster or Gibson SG Standard
guitar.pickup: Neck/middle single coil for glassy intro arpeggios; bridge humbucker for roaring chorus crunch

amp.recommended: Marshall JMP 50W Lead Head paired with Roland JC-120 (for pristine cleans)

effects.distortion: Boss DS-1 or Tube Screamer pushing the Marshall preamp
effects.reverb: Analog plate or spring reverb for haunting spatial depth
effects.other: Boss CE-2 Chorus pedal for the shimmering intro arpeggios

beginner.title: Clean Chord Arpeggios
steps: Master the basic Am, G, and F chord shapes without muted strings
Practice the picking sequence slowly at 80 BPM
Ensure each picked string rings out clearly into the next

intermediate.title: Dynamic Switching & Power Chords
steps: Transition smoothly between the clean intro and crushing chorus power chords
Lock into the 130 BPM tempo with metronome
Execute clean chord stops and mute control

advanced.title: Lyrical Solo & Expressive Touch
steps: Learn Rick Brewster's complete melodic solo note-for-note
Master the expressive whole-step bends on the 10th and 15th frets
Incorporate classical-influenced vibrato into sustained notes

commonMistakes: Collapsing fingers onto adjacent strings during the clean intro arpeggios
Failing to boost volume/gain significantly when entering the explosive chorus
Rushing the tempo during the emotional guitar solo
practiceRoutine: 10 mins: Slow, deliberate arpeggio picking drill on Am-G-F at 90 BPM
10 mins: Dynamic transition drill switching between clean strumming and chorus power crunch
10 mins: Solo bend pitch matching with tuner
5 mins: Full track playthrough focusing on dynamic expression
focusAreas: Left-hand fingertip arching for clean ringing open strings
Dynamic control using guitar volume pot or channel switcher
Pitch precision and singing vibrato on lead lines
metronomeWork: Start arpeggios at 90 BPM focusing on uniform note volume
Advance to 115 BPM synchronizing right-hand alternate picking
Perform at 130 BPM with full emotional and dynamic commitment
